title: Siena no. 9: Castiglione this winter, with the King of Aragon's assent (ASSi Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 9, DECODE R4798)

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 9; DECODE R4798 (Concistoro_2308_52)

plaintext.source: Decipherment of the two cipher passages written below them on the slip in a second hand (manuscript lines 7-8).

transcription.source: George Lasry with CTTS (transcription by Claude, held in CTTS)
transcription.notes: 53 cipher symbols in 3 lines, from the report, not re-measured. The project's 24 Sept transcription (transcripts/no09.txt, 46 tokens, 28 names) was not used for the reading. George Lasry names accurate transcription as the main obstacle in this fascicle.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of single letters: five signs for a, three each for e and o, two each for r, t and u, one for the rest; words set apart by spaces and dot or slash separators; one probable null; two clear code words (Stella = the King of Aragon, nichil = la pratica?) as a small nomenclator (George Lasry's key, 33 signs).
system.sibling_key: none; no fasc. 1 key fits (siena1421 survey)
system.notes: Key figure docs/siena9_key.png (report p. 33). The code words are written as clear Latin/Italian words, not signs.

prior_solution.where: The second hand's decipherment on the slip itself (lines 7-8), covering the two passages; not the final group.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry ran the solution in CTTS with Claude (transcription by Claude; key recovered by Claude from the second hand's decipherment); this project filed his report.
models: Claude (version not stated in the report)

solution.what: Project survey (siena1421): slip transcribed by agent J (46 cipher tokens, 28 names); lines 7-8 taken for clear text in a second hand, with a note that they might be a decipherment.
Project survey: fasc. 1 key alphabets compared by eye; none fits. Closed as too short for ciphertext-only.

George Lasry with CTTS and Claude: the second hand's lines ('uno altro anno', 'Chastiglone questa vernata') identified as the decipherment of the two passages; key recovered from them sign for sign (33 signs).
Both passages read: '[di?] Chastiglone questa vernata', 'uno altro anno'; final group 'Francesco? i?' doubtful; Stella = re d'Aragona from the decipherment.
This project counted the reading: 36 of 44 letter values in the cipher passages without a query (81.8%).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's decryption and translation (lasry_report.md, verbatim), his key as counts (key.md; his key figure is docs/siena9_key.png, outside the folder); transcription = this project's 24 Sept one (transcripts/no09.txt), his CTTS transcription not being in the repository.

validation.notes: contributed reading; key fixed by the contemporary decipherment; 53 symbols, too short for a statistical test

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The report says the key was recovered from the decipherment written on the slip in a second hand, which fixes the two passages sign for sign.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted on George Lasry's reading (lasry_report.md): 36 of 44 letter values in the cipher passages read without a query (Chastiglone questa vernata, uno altro anno); di? and the final group Francesco? i? doubtful; the clear code words not counted.

gaps.detail: nothing on the slip names or dates them; 1440s-50s per George Lasry, unverified

texts.label: No. 9 (R4798), a slip on Castiglione this winter, [1447-48?] (George Lasry)
texts.summary: A slip in Italian clear text with two cipher passages, deciphered in a second hand below them: '[la pratica?] [di?] Chastiglone questa vernata con lo sentimento di [re d'Aragona] e nutrire questa guerra uno altro anno', with a final group read 'Francesco? i?'. George Lasry dates it to the 1440s-1450s (Castiglione held by Alfonso V from 1447; the winter of 1447-48 fits best), unverified. Decryption and translation are his (lasry_report.md); the transcription linked is this project's independent one of 24 Sept 2026, since his CTTS transcription is not in the repository.
